dublinCore.dc:title: 116 HR 4726 IH: Certainty for End-Users Act
dublinCore.dc:rights: Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.

action.action-desc: Mr. Marshall introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Agriculture

form.official-title: To help end-users better utilize derivatives markets by refining the definition of financial entity, clarifying how affiliates can utilize the end-user exception, and harmonizing clearing and margin exemptions.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Certainty for End-Users Act.

subsection.text: Section 2(h) of the Commodity Exchange Act (7 U.S.C. 2(h)) is amended—

paragraph.text: by striking paragraph (1)(A) and inserting the following:

subparagraph.text: It shall be unlawful for a financial entity to engage in a swap with another financial entity, unless the swap is submitted for clearing to a derivatives clearing organization registered under this Act or a derivatives clearing organization exempt from registration under this Act if the swap is required to be cleared.
in the paragraph heading, by striking Exceptions and inserting Application of clearing requirement;
by striking subparagraphs (A) and (B) and redesignating subparagraph (C) as subparagraph (A);

clause.text: by striking clause (i) and inserting the following:
In this subsection, the term financial entity means the following:

item.text: A commodity pool that is required to be operated by a commodity pool operator registered with the Commission, or a foreign person that would be such a commodity pool if the foreign person were organized under the laws of the United States or any State.

An investment company (as defined in section 3 of the Investment Company Act of 1940 (15 U.S.C. 80a–3)), or a foreign person that would be such an investment company if the foreign person were organized under the laws of the United States or any State.

subclause.text: A private fund as defined in section 202(a) of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (15 U.S.C. 80–b–2(a)), or a foreign person that would be such a private fund if the foreign person were organized under the laws of the United States or any State.

Such other persons the Commission determines by rule to be predominantly engaged in activities that are financial in nature. In making such a determination, the Commission may consider section 4(k) of the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956. The Commission shall promulgate regulations to carry out this subclause.

clause.text: in clause (iii), by striking Such definition and inserting The term; and
by adding at the end the following:

subclause.text: A person described in subclause (III), and not subclause (I) or (II), of clause (i) shall not be considered a financial entity for purposes of this subsection if the total swaps activity of the person, when calculated with those of all other affiliated persons who are so described, amount to less than—

item.text: $1,000,000,000 in gross notional swaps transactions calculated on the basis of a rolling 12-month period; or

an alternative de minimis amount of swaps activity, exposure, transactions, or other measurement, as determined by the Commission. At least every 5 years, the Commission shall consider modifying the alternative de minimis amount due to inflation or other market factors.

subclause.text: The calculation under subclause (I) shall not include—

item.text: swaps used to hedge or mitigate risk associated with an asset owned or liability incurred or reasonably likely to be owned or incurred by an entity in the conduct of such entity’s business; or

swaps used by an insurance company for asset replication if they are expressly permitted by State insurance regulators to be entered into in conjunction with other investments in order to replicate the investment characteristics of otherwise permissible investments.

subclause.header: Requirements of entities relying on the de minimis exclusion
subclause.text: An entity that relies on the de minimis exception in this clause to avoid clearing swaps transactions that the Commission requires a financial entity to clear pursuant to paragraph (1)(A) and Commission regulations shall, with respect to the swaps, report or cause to be reported, to a registered swap data repository the reliance of the entity on the de minimis exclusion.

subparagraph.text: by inserting after subparagraph (A) (as amended by the preceding provisions of this paragraph) the following:

subclause.text: 1 of the entities, directly or indirectly, holds a majority ownership interest in the other entity; or
a third party, directly or indirectly, holds a majority ownership interest in both entities.
a person not described in subparagraph (A)(i); or
a person described in clause (ii), (iii), or (iv) of subparagraph (A).

subparagraph.text: A non-financial entity that engages in swaps transactions that the Commission requires a financial entity to clear pursuant to paragraph (1)(A) and Commission regulations shall, with respect to the swaps, report or cause to be reported, to a registered swap data repository their status as a non-financial entity.

section.text: Section 2(h)(7) of the Commodity Exchange Act (7 U.S.C. 2(h)(7)), as amended by section 2 of this Act, is amended—

paragraph.text: by striking subparagraph (D) and inserting the following:

clause.text: The requirements of paragraph (1)(A) shall not apply to a swap entered into by a risk management entity if the swap is—

subclause.text: used to hedge or mitigate eligible risk originating from one or more affiliated non-financial entities; and
not netted, combined, or consolidated with any other swap to which the requirements of paragraph (1)(A) apply.

clause.text: In this subparagraph, the term risk management entity means—

subclause.text: an entity described in subclause (II), and not subclause (I), of subparagraph (A)(i), that enters only into transactions related to the management of eligible risk;
an entity described in only subclause (III) of subparagraph (A)(i); or
a non-financial entity.

clause.text: In this subparagraph, the term eligible risk means risk that—

subclause.text: originates from a non-financial entity;
is associated with an asset owned or liability incurred or reasonably likely to be owned or incurred by the non-financial entity in the conduct of the business of the non-financial entity;
is not netted, combined, or consolidated with risk originating from any affiliated financial entity; and
if transferred, is transferred only to or through one or more affiliated risk management entities.

clause.text: A risk management entity that engages in swaps which utilize the exception in this subparagraph shall—

subclause.text: notify the Commission, in a manner prescribed by the Commission, how the risk management entity generally meets the financial obligations of the risk management entity associated with entering into non-cleared swaps;
identify those swaps used to hedge or mitigate eligible risk originating from one or more affiliated non-financial entities; and

maintain books and records of the swaps which utilize the exception in this subparagraph and the related eligible risk in such form and manner and for such period as may be required by the Commission.

clause.text: Nothing in this subparagraph shall be interpreted to limit the ability of any non-financial entity to engage in a swap to which the requirements of paragraph (1)(A) do not apply.

paragraph.text: by striking subparagraph (F) and inserting the following:

subparagraph.text: The Commission may prescribe such rules or issue such interpretations of the rules as the Commission determines to be necessary to prevent abuse of the exceptions described in this paragraph. The Commission may request information from a person claiming to be a non-financial entity as necessary to prevent evasion of the rules or abuse of the exceptions described in this paragraph.

section.text: Section 4s(e)(4) of the Commodity Exchange Act (7 U.S.C. 6s(e)(4)) is amended to read as follows:

subparagraph.text: Paragraphs (2)(A)(ii) and (2)(B)(ii), including the initial and variation margin requirements imposed under such paragraphs, shall not apply to a swap—

clause.text: in which a counterparty is a non-financial entity (as defined in section 2(h)(7)(B)(ii)), regardless of whether the swap is required to be cleared;
that qualifies for the exception provided in subparagraph (D) of section 2(h)(7), or that would so qualify if the swap were required to be cleared; or
that qualifies for an exception or exemption from the requirements of section 2(h)(1)(A) pursuant to any Commission rule, regulation, or order.

subparagraph.header: Preservation of variation margin exchange requirement applicable to certain insurance companies
subparagraph.text: Notwithstanding subparagraph (A) of this paragraph, if an insurance company would be a financial entity for purposes of section 2(h) if the swaps described in section 2(h)(7)(A)(iv)(II)(bb) of the insurance company were not excluded from the de minimis calculation under section 2(h)(7)(A)(iv), then all swaps of the insurance company shall be subject to the variation margin requirements of paragraphs (2)(A)(ii) and (2)(B)(ii) of this subsection.

section.header: Modification of definition of major swap participant
section.text: Section 1a(33)(A)(iii)(I) of the Commodity Exchange Act (7 U.S.C. 1a(33)(A)(iii)(I)) is amended by inserting , or a non-financial entity that would be considered to be a financial entity for purposes of section 2(h) but for the application of the de minimis exclusion provided for in section 2(h)(7)(A)(iv), before that is highly.
